replacements.reference: Hadvar from Skyrim
replacements.fit: The sun, green eyes, dark hair, and stern mouth give him the practical alertness of a grounded RPG guard.

replacements.reference: Beedle, recurring Zelda merchant
replacements.fit: The ice cream, bright smile, cloud, and high ginger bun make Beedle a cheerful traveling-shopkeeper fit.

replacements.reference: Brewster from Animal Crossing
replacements.fit: The drink glass, black hair, white cloud, and reserved expression strongly suggest a quiet tavern or café proprietor.

replacements.reference: Malo, shopkeeper in Zelda: Twilight Princess
replacements.fit: The lollipop, sun, compact frame, ginger bun, and small smile match a clever young village shopkeeper.

replacements.reference: Bolson, builder NPC in Zelda: Breath of the Wild
replacements.fit: The messy-room scene, proud stance, cool expression, and dramatic bun fit Bolson's colorful village-contractor energy.

replacements.reference: Torneko, merchant from Dragon Quest IV
replacements.fit: The hamburger, sunrise, orange curls, and googly stare create an unmistakable comic RPG merchant silhouette.

replacements.reference: Groose from Zelda: Skyward Sword
replacements.fit: The raised baseball bat, scream, swept dark hair, and blue field suit a loud, boastful adventurer name.

replacements.reference: Wyll, the Blade of Frontiers from Baldur's Gate 3
replacements.fit: The dark complexion, basketball, closed eyes, and confident smile give him a heroic athletic presence.

replacements.reference: Zack Fair from Final Fantasy VII
replacements.fit: The baseball, raised gaze, bright smile, cloudy field, and wild red hair match an energetic young RPG hero.

replacements.reference: Tingle from The Legend of Zelda
replacements.fit: The sour scream, rough light hair, soccer ball, and pink field have exactly the oddball village-character energy Tingle needs.

replacements.reference: Sherb, goat villager from Animal Crossing
replacements.fit: The happy eyes, soft red curls, ice cream, and blue field make this an easygoing cozy-villager portrait.

replacements.reference: Ralof from Skyrim
replacements.fit: The angry brows, red solar field, yellow brush, and bristling red hair give him a fiery Nord-warrior read.

replacements.reference: Belethor, Whiterun merchant in Skyrim
replacements.fit: The baguette, sour eyes, rough hair, and hunched pose suit a slightly weary general-goods merchant.

replacements.reference: Minsc from Baldur's Gate
replacements.fit: The taco, angry brows, mad mouth, purple field, and high dreads create a comic battle-ready RPG figure.

replacements.reference: Alvor, Riverwood blacksmith in Skyrim
replacements.fit: The sturdy stance, ginger bun, red background, and nervous laugh feel like a friendly working village smith.

replacements.reference: Pierre, Pelican Town shopkeeper in Stardew Valley
replacements.fit: The baguette, proud smile, dark hair, and violet shop-sign palette make Pierre an exact small-town merchant fit.

replacements.reference: Alfyn Greengrass, village apothecary in Octopath Traveler
replacements.fit: Green eyes, bright banana hair, a warm smile, and sunrise scenery give him a wholesome healer-villager read.

replacements.reference: Lucan Valerius, Riverwood trader in Skyrim
replacements.fit: The tidy dark hair, warm complexion, red field, and open smile suit a dependable village trader.

replacements.reference: Barcus Wroot from Baldur's Gate 3
replacements.fit: The red sweep, sad beard, swamp spiral, and hamburger burden give him a put-upon inventor-NPC quality.

replacements.reference: Ingo, ranch worker in Zelda: Ocarina of Time
replacements.fit: The happy mustache, green eyes, dark hair, and taco prop read immediately as a lively ranch or stable worker.

replacements.reference: Willy, Pelican Town fisherman in Stardew Valley
replacements.fit: The drink, cloud, flat gaze, and windblown gold hair suggest an easygoing dockside tavern regular.

replacements.reference: Zevran from Dragon Age: Origins
replacements.fit: The sideways sour eyes, laughing mouth, dark hair, and blue field give him a sly rogue's charm.

replacements.reference: Fritz, farmer from Story of Seasons
replacements.fit: The red frizz, laugh, and vivid spiral background make Fritz feel like a chaotic but lovable farm-town rival.

replacements.reference: Fargoth, Seyda Neen villager in Morrowind
replacements.fit: The rough pale hair, swamp backdrop, brown tilt, and mad mouth create a memorable eccentric-villager face.

replacements.reference: Kass, traveling bard in Zelda: Breath of the Wild
replacements.fit: The proud expression, soft-serve prop, brown hair, and festival spiral suit a colorful wandering bard.

replacements.reference: Ravio, masked merchant in Zelda: A Link Between Worlds
replacements.fit: The crescent moon, black hair, smile, and scarlet field fit a secretive nighttime merchant better than a heavy gothic name.

replacements.reference: Rolan, tiefling wizard in Baldur's Gate 3
replacements.fit: The frightened upward eyes, scream, ginger bun, and white cloud capture an ambitious apprentice caught in trouble.

replacements.reference: Sidon from The Legend of Zelda
replacements.fit: The ocean-blue background, cloud, red frizz, and bright prop create an aquatic heroic color story.

replacements.reference: Mayor Lewis from Stardew Valley
replacements.fit: The compact mustache, baguette, closed eyes, and village-festival spiral make Lewis a natural mayoral NPC.

replacements.reference: Kilton, nocturnal monster merchant in Zelda: Breath of the Wild
replacements.fit: The crescent moon, dark face, high bun, ice cream, and mad expression make Kilton the batch's clearest night-shop character.

replacements.reference: Recurring engineer Cid from Final Fantasy
replacements.fit: The white brush, grey stare, black hair, and laugh give him the practical eccentricity of a recurring RPG engineer.

replacements.reference: Vesemir from The Witcher
replacements.fit: The long beard, rough pale hair, sour gaze, and overgrown landscape make Vesemir an exceptionally direct veteran-mentor fit.

replacements.reference: Apollo, eagle villager from Animal Crossing
replacements.fit: The sunrise, soccer ball, round eyes, and high bun give him a bold outdoorsy villager silhouette.

replacements.reference: Lucky, dog villager from Animal Crossing
replacements.fit: The baseball, raised bat, startled smile, and orange curls make Lucky a playful sports-name connection.

replacements.reference: Yangus from Dragon Quest VIII
replacements.fit: The soccer ball, sun, wild orange hair, googly eyes, and grimace fit a broad comic adventurer rather than the generic Quest.

replacements.reference: Zoltan Chivay from The Witcher
replacements.fit: The beer, overgrown scenery, grey stare, laugh, and orange curls give him the sociable toughness of a fantasy tavern regular.

replacements.reference: Varric Tethras from Dragon Age
replacements.fit: The dark complexion, red frizz, bright smile, and clean blue field suit a charismatic storyteller and companion.

replacements.reference: Therion from Octopath Traveler
replacements.fit: The rough blond hair, upward eyes, mad mouth, and pink field give him a sharp, impatient thief-NPC edge.

replacements.reference: Harris from Harvest Moon: Back to Nature
replacements.fit: The berry cake, proud expression, round eyes, and rough blond hair suit a familiar small-town game character rather than a fantasy title.
